notes: Corner numbers are now the track's real corners, not a guess. Lap history used to find corners in your speed trace, so the numbering changed depending on which lap you compared against - across 31 laps at Spa that produced 29 different sets of corners, and T8 was not the same corner from one lap to the next. Corners now come from community track data with their real names: T1 La Source, T2 Eau Rouge, T5 Les Combes, T13 Blanchimont, the same for every lap and every comparison. The racing line is drawn as a curve instead of straight segments, so it follows the track instead of cutting across corners - and because that is only drawing, every lap you already have is smoothed too. Corner advice is back on older laps: it had been switched off for every lap recorded before the measured-time format, so you saw a number next to an empty advice card. Five interface styles now genuinely change the app - typography, uppercase, card shapes and spacing, not just a different shade - and each card takes its border and fill from its own accent colour. Settings are laid out in fields with a hover explanation for each one. Under the hood, the time reconstruction no longer depends on how finely a lap was stored, which had been making corner losses wrong once laps of different detail lived in the same file. Much of this was verified by reading the code, on your own stored laps and in demo mode rather than out on track, so if the engineer says something odd out there, please use the feedback form in the app.
